From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

(Redirected from [Publishers](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishers&redirect=no "Publishers"))

Production and distribution of media

"Publisher" redirects here. For other uses, see [Publisher (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publisher_(disambiguation) "Publisher (disambiguation)").

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Shelves_of_titles_at_the_Aboriginal_Studies_Press_bookshop.jpg/250px-Shelves_of_titles_at_the_Aboriginal_Studies_Press_bookshop.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shelves_of_titles_at_the_Aboriginal_Studies_Press_bookshop.jpg)

The [Aboriginal Studies Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_Studies_Press "Aboriginal Studies Press") (ASP) bookshop at the [Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Institute_of_Aboriginal_and_Torres_Strait_Islander_Studies "Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies")

**[Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishing)** is the process of making information, literature, music, software, and other content, whether in physical or digital form, available to the public for sale or free of charge.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-1) Traditionally, the term publishing refers to the creation and distribution of [printed works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Printing "Printing"), such as [books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book "Book"), [zines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zine "Zine"), [comic books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_book "Comic book"), [newspapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newspaper "Newspaper"), and [magazines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magazine "Magazine"), to the public. The advent of digital information systems has led to an expansion of its scope to include [digital publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_publishing "Electronic publishing"), such as [e-books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-book "E-book"), [digital magazines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magazines "Magazines"), [websites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_publishing "Electronic publishing"), [social media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media "Social media"), [music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music "Music"), and [video game publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_publisher "Video game publisher").

The commercial publishing industry ranges from large multinational conglomerates such as [News Corp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/News_Corp "News Corp"), [Pearson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearson_PLC "Pearson PLC"), [Penguin Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Random_House "Penguin Random House"), and [Thomson Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomson_Reuters "Thomson Reuters")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-2) to major retail brands and thousands of [small independent publishers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_press "Small press"). It has various divisions such as trade/retail publishing of fiction and non-fiction, educational publishing, and [academic and scientific publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_publishing "Academic publishing").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-3) Publishing is also undertaken by governments, civil society, and private companies for administrative or compliance requirements, business, research, advocacy, or public interest objectives.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-4) This can include [annual reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annual_report "Annual report"), [research reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_reports "Research reports"), [market research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_research "Market research"), policy briefings, and [technical reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_report "Technical report").

Publishing has evolved from a small, ancient form limited by law or religion to a modern, large-scale industry disseminating all types of information.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-5)

"**Publisher**" can refer to a publishing company, an organization, or an individual who leads a publishing company, [imprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imprint_(trade_name) "Imprint (trade name)"), [periodical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodical_literature "Periodical literature"), or newspaper.

2.   [Writing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writer "Writer")

6.   [Typesetting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typesetting "Typesetting")
7.   [Proofreading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proofreading "Proofreading")
8.   [Correction cycles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proofreading "Proofreading")
9.   [Indexing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Index_(publishing) "Index (publishing)")

## Types of publishers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Types of publishers")]

### Newspaper publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Newspaper publishing")]

[Newspapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newspaper "Newspaper") and [news websites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_newspaper "Online newspaper") publish current reports, [articles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_(publishing) "Article (publishing)"), and [features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feature_story "Feature story") written by [journalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journalist "Journalist"). They are available through individual purchases, paid [subscriptions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subscription_business_model "Subscription business model"), or for free. These publications feature photographs or other media, and they are usually subsidized with [advertising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising "Advertising"). They generally cover [local](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_news "Local news"), national, and international news, or feature a particular industry. Some organizations charge premium fees if they have expertise and exclusive knowledge. The news industry is meant to serve the public interest, hold people and businesses accountable, and promote freedom of information and expression.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-7) Editors manage the tone of their publication; for example, negative versus positive articles can affect the reader's perspective.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-8)

### Journal publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Journal publishing")]

A [journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_journal "Academic journal") is an academic or technical publication available in digital, print, or both formats, containing articles written by researchers, professors, and industry experts. These publications are specific to a particular field and often push the boundaries established within that discipline. To ensure validity and high quality, they usually require submissions to undergo [peer review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review "Peer review").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-9)

### Magazine publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Magazine publishing")]

A [magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magazine "Magazine") is a periodical published at regular intervals. It features creative layouts, photography, and illustrations that cover a particular subject or interest. Magazines are available in print or digital formats, and they can be purchased individually or as a subscription.

### Book publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Book publishing")]

![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Split-arrows.svg/60px-Split-arrows.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)It has been suggested that this section be [**split**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Splitting "Wikipedia:Splitting") out into another article titled _[Book publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book\_publishing "Book publishing")_. ([**Discuss**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Publishing "Talk:Publishing")) _(March 2026)_

The global book publishing industry consists of books categorized as [fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiction "Fiction") or [non-fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fiction "Non-fiction") and [print](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book "Book"), [e-book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebook "Ebook"), or [audiobook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audiobook "Audiobook"). The book market is huge, with around 1.5 billion people speaking English.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-10) Translation services are also available to make these texts accessible in other languages. Self-publishing makes publishing widely accessible through small print-run [digital printing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_printing "Digital printing") or online self-publishing platforms. [E-reader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-reader "E-reader") screen technology continues to improve with increased contrast and resolution making them more comfortable to read. Each book has a registered [ISBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISBN "ISBN") to identify it.

### Directory publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Directory publishing")]

[Directories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_directory "Web directory") contain searchable indexed data about businesses, products, and services. They were printed in the past but are now mostly online. Directories are available as searchable lists, on a map, as a sector-specific [portal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_portal "Web portal"), as a [review site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_site "Review site") (expert or consumer), or as a [comparison site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_shopping_website "Comparison shopping website"). Although some businesses may not consider themselves publishers, the way the data is displayed is published.

### Textbook publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Textbook publishing")]

A [textbook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Textbook "Textbook") is an educational book, or e-book, that contains information on a particular subject and is used by people studying that subject.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-11) The need for textbook publishing continues due to the global need for education.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-13) Textbooks from major publishers are being integrated with online learning platforms for expert knowledge and access to a library of books with digital content.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-14) A [university press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_press "University press") is an academic publisher run by a university. [Oxford University Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Press "Oxford University Press") is the largest in the world and specializes in research, education, and English language teaching internationally.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-15)

### Catalog publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Catalog publishing")]

A catalog is a visual directory or list of a large range of products that allow you to browse and buy from a particular company.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-16) In print, this is usually in the format of a softback book or directory. Smaller visual catalogs can be known as brochures. With the Internet, they have evolved into searchable databases of products known under the term [e-commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-commerce "E-commerce"). Interactive catalogs and brochures like IKEA[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-17) and Avon[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-18) allow customers to browse a full range if they have not decided on their purchase. Responsive web and app design will allow further integration between interactive catalog visuals and searchable product databases.

### Web publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Web publishing")]

Until recently, physical books were the primary source of recording knowledge. For accessibility and global reach, this content can be repurposed for the web. The [British Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Library "British Library"), for example, holds more than 170 million items with 3 million new additions each year.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-19) With consent, content can be published online through e-books, audio books, [CMS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_management_system "Content management system")-based websites, online learning platforms, videos, or mobile apps. On the Internet, writers and copy editors are known as content writers and content editors, although their roles vary from their print-based counterparts.

### Advertising

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Advertising")]

Advertising can provide income or a subsidized income for publishers. If the advertising has a [return on investment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return_on_investment "Return on investment") (ROI), the publisher can boost income exponentially by increasing the spending. An ROI of up to £10 per £1 invested is possible, as seen in the John Lewis & Partners [Christmas campaigns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lewis_Christmas_advert "John Lewis Christmas advert").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-21) Likewise, any cost savings that harm the customer/consumer experience can impact a brand in the long term. [Multichannel marketing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multichannel_marketing "Multichannel marketing") can be more cost-effective in creating an immersive experience that cannot be replicated with one channel. For example, when considering marketing spend, a shop with a small margin (or none at all) compared to a website is very cost-effective because it acts as a huge billboard that offers a browsing experience that enables consumers to make purchasing decisions. It gives them a feel for the brand, has a presence in the community, and creates jobs. Also, using social media publishing to advertise has a good ROI if trending, high-quality content is created that reflects positively on the brand.

### Tie-in publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Tie-in publishing")]

Main article: [Tie-in](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tie-in "Tie-in")

Film, television, radio, and advertisements publish information to their audiences. Computer games, streaming apps, and social media publish content in various ways that can keep audiences more engaged. Marketing additional products closely related to a major film, such as _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_, is an example of tie-in publishing. These products include but are not limited to spin-off books, graphic novels, soundtrack albums, computer games, models and toys, social media posts, and promotional publications. Examples of tie-in publishing based on books are the _[Harry Potter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter "Harry Potter")_ and _[James Bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James\_Bond "James Bond")_ franchises.

See also: [Periodical publication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodical_publication "Periodical publication")

## Book publishing sub-divisions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Book publishing sub-divisions")]

See also: [History of books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_books "History of books")

"Book publishing company" redirects here. For the publisher named Book Publishing Company, see [The Farm (Tennessee)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Farm_(Tennessee) "The Farm (Tennessee)").

![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Split-arrows.svg/60px-Split-arrows.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)It has been suggested that this section be [**split**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Splitting "Wikipedia:Splitting") out into another article titled _[Book publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book\_publishing "Book publishing")_. ([**Discuss**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Publishing "Talk:Publishing")) _(March 2026)_
[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/2023-2024-Key-Book-Publishing-Paths-by-Jane-Friedman-1000x647.png/250px-2023-2024-Key-Book-Publishing-Paths-by-Jane-Friedman-1000x647.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2023-2024-Key-Book-Publishing-Paths-by-Jane-Friedman-1000x647.png)

The publishing landscape is continually evolving. Currently there are four major types of publishers in book publishing:[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-22)

### Mainstream publishers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Mainstream publishers")]

These companies traditionally produce hardcopy books in large print runs. They have established networks which distribute those books to bricks-and-mortar stores and libraries.

When a mainstream publisher accepts a book for publication, they require the author to sign a contract surrendering some rights to the publisher. In exchange, the publisher will take care of all aspects of publishing the book at the publisher's cost. They rely entirely on sales of the book to recoup those costs and make a profit. The author receives a royalty on each sale (and sometimes an advance on royalties when the book is accepted[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-23)). Because of the [financial risk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_risk "Financial risk"), mainstream publishers are extremely selective in what they will publish, and reject most manuscripts submitted to them.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-24)

In 2013, [Penguin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Group "Penguin Group") (owned by [Pearson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longman "Longman")) and [Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random_House "Random House") (owned by [Bertelsmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertelsmann_Stiftung "Bertelsmann Stiftung")) merged, narrowing the mainstream publishing industry to a handful of big publishers as it adapted to digital media.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-Penguin_Random_House_to_Buy_Simon_&_Schuster-25) The merger created the largest consumer book publisher globally, with a global market share of more than 25 percent.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-26)As of 2022[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit), approximately 80% percent of the United States trade market for books was controlled by the "**Big Five**" publishing houses: [Penguin Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Random_House "Penguin Random House"), [Hachette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hachette_Book_Group_USA "Hachette Book Group USA"), [HarperCollins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HarperCollins "HarperCollins"), [Simon & Schuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_&_Schuster "Simon & Schuster"), and [Macmillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macmillan_Publishers "Macmillan Publishers").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-27)

In November 2020, ViacomCBS agreed to sell Simon & Schuster, the third largest book publisher in the United States, to Penguin Random House in a deal that, if it had gone through, would have formed the largest publishing company in the world.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-Penguin_Random_House_to_Buy_Simon_&_Schuster-25) On November 2, 2021, the [United States Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice "United States Department of Justice") filed a lawsuit (U.S. v. Bertelsmann SE & CO. KGaA, et al.) to block the merger on antitrust grounds,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-28) and on October 31, 2022, the [D.C. District Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_District_Court_for_the_District_of_Columbia "United States District Court for the District of Columbia") ruled in favor of the Department of Justice, filing a permanent injunction on the merger.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-Judge_Blocks_a_Merger_of_Penguin_Random_House_and_Simon_&_Schuster-29)

Although newspaper and magazine companies still often own printing presses and binderies, book publishers rarely do.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Similarly, the trade usually sells the finished products through a [distributor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distribution_(business) "Distribution (business)") who stores and distributes the publisher's wares for a percentage fee or sells on a sale or return basis.

Some major publishers have entire divisions devoted to a single franchise, e.g., Ballantine [Del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Del_Rey_Books "Del Rey Books") LucasBooks has the exclusive rights to _Star Wars_ in the United States; Random House UK (Bertelsmann)/Century LucasBooks holds the same rights in the United Kingdom. The [video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") industry self-publishes through BL Publishing/[Black Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Library "Black Library") ([_Warhammer_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warhammer_Fantasy_(setting) "Warhammer Fantasy (setting)")) and Wizards of the Coast (_[Dragonlance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragonlance "Dragonlance")_, _[Forgotten Realms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forgotten\_Realms "Forgotten Realms")_, etc.). The [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") has its own publishing division that does very well with long-running series such as _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Who "Doctor Who")_. These multimedia works are cross-marketed aggressively, and sales frequently outperform the average stand-alone published work, making them a focus of corporate interest.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-cave-30)

The advent of the [Internet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet "Internet") has provided an alternative mode of book distribution and most mainstream publishers also offer their books in ebook format. Preparing a book for e-book publication is the same as print publication, with only minor variations in the process to account for the different publishing mediums; E-book publication also eliminates some costs like the discount given to retailers (usually around 45 percent).[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-ireaderreview.com-31)

### Small presses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Small presses")]

Small publishers, also called independent or indie publishers,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-32) operate on a traditional model (i.e. the author surrenders some rights in exchange for the publisher bearing all costs of publishing), but their precise terms can vary greatly.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-33) Often, they do not pay an advance on royalties.

### [Hybrid publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_publishing "Hybrid publishing")

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Hybrid publishing")]

A hybrid publisher shares the costs of publication (and therefore the risks) with the author. Because of this financial risk, they are selective in what they publish. The contract varies according to what is negotiated between author and company, but will always include the surrender of some rights to the publisher.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-34) Hybrid publishing is the source of debate in the publishing industry, due to the tendency of vanity presses to masquerade as hybrids.

### [Vanity presses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity_press "Vanity press")

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Vanity presses")]

A vanity press will publish any book. In return, the author must cover all the costs of publication, surrender some rights to the publisher, and pay royalties on sales. Vanity presses often engage in deceptive practices or offer costly, poor-quality services with limited recourse available to the writer. In the US, these practices have been cited by the [Better Business Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Better_Business_Bureau "Better Business Bureau") as unfavorable reports by consumers.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-35) Given the bad reputation of vanity publishing, many vanity presses brand themselves as hybrid publishers. The Society of Authors (SoA) and the Writers' Guild of Great Britain (WGGB) have called for reform of the paid-for publishing sector. These unions, representing 14,800 authors, jointly published a report to expose widespread bad practices among companies that charge writers to publish their work while taking away their rights.

### [Self-publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-publishing "Self-publishing")

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Self-publishing")]

When an author self-publishes a book, they retain all rights and assume responsibility for all stages of preparing, publishing and distributing the book. The author may hire professionals on a fee-for-service basis as needed, (e.g. an editor, cover designer, proofreader) or engage a company to provide an integrated package.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-36)

## Recent developments

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Recent developments")]

[Accessible publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accessible_publishing "Accessible publishing") uses the digitization of books to mark them up into [XML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XML "XML") and produce multiple formats to sell to customers, often targeting those who experience difficulty reading. Formats include a variety of larger print sizes, specialized print formats for [dyslexia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dyslexia "Dyslexia"),[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-37) eye tracking problems, and [macular degeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macular_degeneration "Macular degeneration"), as well as [Braille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braille "Braille"), [DAISY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_accessible_information_system "Digital accessible information system"), [audiobooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audiobook "Audiobook"), and [e-books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-books "E-books").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-38)

Green publishing means adapting the publishing process to minimize environmental impact. One example is the concept of on-demand printing, using digital or print-on-demand technology. This cuts down the need to ship books since they are manufactured close to the customer on a just-in-time basis.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-39)

A further development is the growth of online publishing, where no physical books are produced. The author creates an e-book and uploads it to a website, from which anyone can download and read it.

An increasing number of authors are using [niche marketing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niche_marketing "Niche marketing") online to sell more books by engaging with their readers online.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-40)

Some publishers can show political [homophily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homophily "Homophily") or [political bias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_bias "Political bias").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-p016-41)

## Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

Main article: [Publication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publication "Publication")

Publication is the distribution of copies or [content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_(media_and_publishing) "Content (media and publishing)") to the [public](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_public "General public").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-bc-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-ucc-45) The [Berne Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berne_Convention_for_the_Protection_of_Literary_and_Artistic_Works "Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works") requires that this can only be done with the consent of the copyright holder, which initially is always the author.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-bc-44) In the [Universal Copyright Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Copyright_Convention "Universal Copyright Convention"), "publication" is defined in Article VI as "the reproduction in tangible form and the general distribution to the public of copies of a work from which it can be read or otherwise visually perceived."[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-ucc-45)

## Privishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Privishing")]

**Privishing** (_priv_ ate publ _ishing_, but not to be confused with [self-publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-publishing "Self-publishing")) is a modern term for publishing a book but printing so few copies or with such lack of marketing, advertising, or sales support that it effectively does not reach the public.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-46) The book, while nominally published, is almost impossible to obtain through normal channels such as bookshops, often cannot be ordered specially, and has a notable lack of support from its publisher, including refusal to reprint the title. A book that is privished may be referred to as "killed". Depending on the motivation, privishing may constitute a [breach of contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breach_of_contract "Breach of contract"), [censorship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Censorship "Censorship"),[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-47) or good business practice (e.g., not printing more books than the publisher believes will sell in a reasonable length of time).

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/The_Caxton_Celebration_-_William_Caxton_showing_specimens_of_his_printing_to_King_Edward_IV_and_his_Queen.jpg/330px-The_Caxton_Celebration_-_William_Caxton_showing_specimens_of_his_printing_to_King_Edward_IV_and_his_Queen.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Caxton_Celebration_-_William_Caxton_showing_specimens_of_his_printing_to_King_Edward_IV_and_his_Queen.jpg)

Printer working an early [Gutenberg letterpress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gutenberg_letter_press "Gutenberg letter press") from the 15th century (1877 engraving)

Publishing became possible with the [invention of writing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_writing "History of writing") and became more practical upon the [introduction of printing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_printing "History of printing"). Before printing, distributed works were copied manually by [scribes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scribe "Scribe"). Due to printing, publishing progressed hand-in-hand with the [development of books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_books "History of books").

The Chinese inventor [Bi Sheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bi_Sheng "Bi Sheng") made a [movable type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movable_type "Movable type") of earthenware c.1045, but there are no known surviving examples of his work. The Korean civil servant [Ch'oe Yun-ŭi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch'oe_Yun-%C5%ADi "Ch'oe Yun-ŭi"), who lived during the [Goryeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goryeo "Goryeo") Dynasty, invented the first metal moveable type in 1234–1250 AD.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-48)

### Europe

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Europe")]

[Johannes Gutenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_Gutenberg "Johannes Gutenberg") developed movable type in Europe around 1450, along with innovations in casting the type based on a matrix and [hand mould](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hand_mould "Hand mould"). The invention of the [printing press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Printing_press "Printing press") gradually made books less expensive to produce and more widely available.

Early printed books, single sheets, and images created before 1501 in Europe are known as [incunables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incunable "Incunable") or _incunabula_. "A man born in 1453, the year of the [fall of Constantinople](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_Constantinople "Fall of Constantinople"), could look back from his fiftieth year on a lifetime in which about eight million books had been printed, more perhaps than all the scribes of Europe had produced since [Constantine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constantine_the_Great "Constantine the Great") founded his city in A.D. 330."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-49)

The [history of modern newspaper publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_newspaper_publishing "History of newspaper publishing") started in Germany in 1609, with the publication [of magazines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magazine#History "Magazine") following in 1663.

Historians describe the last third of the eighteenth century of the German book trade as the _Sturm und Drang_ period, German for "storm and stress."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-50)

Missionaries brought printing presses to [sub-Saharan Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-Saharan_Africa "Sub-Saharan Africa") in the mid-18th century.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-51)

Historically, publishing has been handled by publishers, although some authors self-published.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-52)

### United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: United States")]

Further information: [Books in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Books_in_the_United_States "Books in the United States") and [A History of the Book in America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_History_of_the_Book_in_America "A History of the Book in America")

The US publishing industry began with a printing press in Massachusetts in 1638, establishing New England as an early hub. Philadelphia also became significant, with [William Bradford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Bradford_(printer,_born_1663) "William Bradford (printer, born 1663)") setting up the first paper mill and [Benjamin Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Franklin "Benjamin Franklin") opening his own press. By the mid-19th century, New York City became the industry's center, marked by the rise of large publishing houses like [Harper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harper_(publisher) "Harper (publisher)"), [Wiley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley_(publisher) "Wiley (publisher)"), [Putnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G._P._Putnam's_Sons "G. P. Putnam's Sons"), and [Scribner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Scribner's_Sons "Charles Scribner's Sons"), who benefited from copyright laws and new distribution methods. Initially, they heavily relied on pirated British works until [international copyright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_copyright "International copyright") laws were established in 1891.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-53) The mid-19th century also saw innovations like paperback "dime novels" making literature more accessible.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-54) The post-World War I era was a boom for American publishing with new writers and publishers like [Simon & Schuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_&_Schuster "Simon & Schuster") and [Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random_House "Random House") emerging. The Great Depression caused a setback, but the industry recovered post-war. Since the 1960s, there's been a trend of mergers and consolidation, accelerating with the rise of online retailers and ebooks, though New York City remains a major global publishing center, home to the "Big Five" publishers (including [HarperCollins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HarperCollins "HarperCollins"), [Penguin Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Random_House "Penguin Random House"), and [Simon & Schuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_&_Schuster "Simon & Schuster")) and major educational publishers like [Macmillan Learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macmillan_Learning "Macmillan Learning"), [McGraw-Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McGraw-Hill_Education "McGraw-Hill Education"), [Scholastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scholastic_Corporation "Scholastic Corporation"), and [Wiley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley_(publisher) "Wiley (publisher)"), alongside numerous independent publishers.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-55) Starting with [Cornell University Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_University_Press "Cornell University Press") in 1869 and [Johns Hopkins University Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University_Press "Johns Hopkins University Press") in 1878, many universities set up publishing houses to publish scholarly books and journals of this sort produced by their faculty and graduate students. In the 21st century, however, financial pressures. have been reducing their output.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-56)

A U.S.-based study in 2016 that surveyed 34 publishers found that straight, able-bodied, white females overwhelmingly represent the publishing industry in the US.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-57)[_Salon_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salon_(website) "Salon (website)") described the situation as a "lack of diversity behind the scenes in book world."[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-58) A survey in 2020 by the same group found there has been no significant statistical change in the lack of diversity since the 2016 survey.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-59) Lack of diversity in the American publishing industry has been an issue for years. Within the industry, the least amount of diversity was in higher-level editorial positions.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-60)

### Internet Age

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Internet Age")]

The [establishment of the World Wide Web](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_World_Wide_Web "History of the World Wide Web") in 1989 soon propelled the [website](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Website "Website") into a dominant publishing medium. [Wikis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_wikis "History of wikis") and [blogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_blogging "History of blogging") soon developed, followed by [online books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_book "Online book"), [online newspapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_newspaper#History "Online newspaper"), and [online magazines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_magazine "Online magazine"). This also facilitated the [technological convergence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technological_convergence "Technological convergence") of commercial and self-published content and the convergence of publishing and production into [online production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_producer "Online producer") through the development of [multimedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multimedia "Multimedia") content.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

(Redirected from [Publishers](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishers&redirect=no "Publishers"))

Production and distribution of media

"Publisher" redirects here. For other uses, see [Publisher (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publisher_(disambiguation) "Publisher (disambiguation)").

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Shelves_of_titles_at_the_Aboriginal_Studies_Press_bookshop.jpg/250px-Shelves_of_titles_at_the_Aboriginal_Studies_Press_bookshop.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shelves_of_titles_at_the_Aboriginal_Studies_Press_bookshop.jpg)

The [Aboriginal Studies Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_Studies_Press "Aboriginal Studies Press") (ASP) bookshop at the [Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Institute_of_Aboriginal_and_Torres_Strait_Islander_Studies "Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies")

**[Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishing)** is the process of making information, literature, music, software, and other content, whether in physical or digital form, available to the public for sale or free of charge.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-1) Traditionally, the term publishing refers to the creation and distribution of [printed works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Printing "Printing"), such as [books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book "Book"), [zines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zine "Zine"), [comic books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_book "Comic book"), [newspapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newspaper "Newspaper"), and [magazines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magazine "Magazine"), to the public. The advent of digital information systems has led to an expansion of its scope to include [digital publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_publishing "Electronic publishing"), such as [e-books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-book "E-book"), [digital magazines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magazines "Magazines"), [websites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_publishing "Electronic publishing"), [social media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media "Social media"), [music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music "Music"), and [video game publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_publisher "Video game publisher").

The commercial publishing industry ranges from large multinational conglomerates such as [News Corp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/News_Corp "News Corp"), [Pearson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearson_PLC "Pearson PLC"), [Penguin Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Random_House "Penguin Random House"), and [Thomson Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomson_Reuters "Thomson Reuters")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-2) to major retail brands and thousands of [small independent publishers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_press "Small press"). It has various divisions such as trade/retail publishing of fiction and non-fiction, educational publishing, and [academic and scientific publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_publishing "Academic publishing").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-3) Publishing is also undertaken by governments, civil society, and private companies for administrative or compliance requirements, business, research, advocacy, or public interest objectives.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-4) This can include [annual reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annual_report "Annual report"), [research reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_reports "Research reports"), [market research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_research "Market research"), policy briefings, and [technical reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_report "Technical report").

Publishing has evolved from a small, ancient form limited by law or religion to a modern, large-scale industry disseminating all types of information.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-5)

"**Publisher**" can refer to a publishing company, an organization, or an individual who leads a publishing company, [imprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imprint_(trade_name) "Imprint (trade name)"), [periodical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodical_literature "Periodical literature"), or newspaper.

2.   [Writing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writer "Writer")

6.   [Typesetting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typesetting "Typesetting")

9.   [Indexing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Index_(publishing) "Index (publishing)")

## Types of publishers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Types of publishers")]

### Newspaper publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Newspaper publishing")]

[Newspapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newspaper "Newspaper") and [news websites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_newspaper "Online newspaper") publish current reports, [articles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_(publishing) "Article (publishing)"), and [features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feature_story "Feature story") written by [journalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journalist "Journalist"). They are available through individual purchases, paid [subscriptions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subscription_business_model "Subscription business model"), or for free. These publications feature photographs or other media, and they are usually subsidized with [advertising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertising "Advertising"). They generally cover [local](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_news "Local news"), national, and international news, or feature a particular industry. Some organizations charge premium fees if they have expertise and exclusive knowledge. The news industry is meant to serve the public interest, hold people and businesses accountable, and promote freedom of information and expression.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-7) Editors manage the tone of their publication; for example, negative versus positive articles can affect the reader's perspective.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-8)

### Journal publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Journal publishing")]

A [journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_journal "Academic journal") is an academic or technical publication available in digital, print, or both formats, containing articles written by researchers, professors, and industry experts. These publications are specific to a particular field and often push the boundaries established within that discipline. To ensure validity and high quality, they usually require submissions to undergo [peer review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review "Peer review").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-9)

### Magazine publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Magazine publishing")]

A [magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magazine "Magazine") is a periodical published at regular intervals. It features creative layouts, photography, and illustrations that cover a particular subject or interest. Magazines are available in print or digital formats, and they can be purchased individually or as a subscription.

### Book publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Book publishing")]

![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Split-arrows.svg/60px-Split-arrows.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)It has been suggested that this section be [**split**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Splitting "Wikipedia:Splitting") out into another article titled _[Book publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book\_publishing "Book publishing")_. ([**Discuss**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Publishing "Talk:Publishing")) _(March 2026)_

The global book publishing industry consists of books categorized as [fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiction "Fiction") or [non-fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fiction "Non-fiction") and [print](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book "Book"), [e-book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebook "Ebook"), or [audiobook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audiobook "Audiobook"). The book market is huge, with around 1.5 billion people speaking English.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-10) Translation services are also available to make these texts accessible in other languages. Self-publishing makes publishing widely accessible through small print-run [digital printing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_printing "Digital printing") or online self-publishing platforms. [E-reader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-reader "E-reader") screen technology continues to improve with increased contrast and resolution making them more comfortable to read. Each book has a registered [ISBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISBN "ISBN") to identify it.

### Directory publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Directory publishing")]

[Directories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_directory "Web directory") contain searchable indexed data about businesses, products, and services. They were printed in the past but are now mostly online. Directories are available as searchable lists, on a map, as a sector-specific [portal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_portal "Web portal"), as a [review site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_site "Review site") (expert or consumer), or as a [comparison site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_shopping_website "Comparison shopping website"). Although some businesses may not consider themselves publishers, the way the data is displayed is published.

### Textbook publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Textbook publishing")]

A [textbook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Textbook "Textbook") is an educational book, or e-book, that contains information on a particular subject and is used by people studying that subject.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-11) The need for textbook publishing continues due to the global need for education.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-13) Textbooks from major publishers are being integrated with online learning platforms for expert knowledge and access to a library of books with digital content.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-14) A [university press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_press "University press") is an academic publisher run by a university. [Oxford University Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Press "Oxford University Press") is the largest in the world and specializes in research, education, and English language teaching internationally.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-15)

### Catalog publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Catalog publishing")]

A catalog is a visual directory or list of a large range of products that allow you to browse and buy from a particular company.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-16) In print, this is usually in the format of a softback book or directory. Smaller visual catalogs can be known as brochures. With the Internet, they have evolved into searchable databases of products known under the term [e-commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-commerce "E-commerce"). Interactive catalogs and brochures like IKEA[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-17) and Avon[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-18) allow customers to browse a full range if they have not decided on their purchase. Responsive web and app design will allow further integration between interactive catalog visuals and searchable product databases.

### Web publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Web publishing")]

Until recently, physical books were the primary source of recording knowledge. For accessibility and global reach, this content can be repurposed for the web. The [British Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Library "British Library"), for example, holds more than 170 million items with 3 million new additions each year.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-19) With consent, content can be published online through e-books, audio books, [CMS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_management_system "Content management system")-based websites, online learning platforms, videos, or mobile apps. On the Internet, writers and copy editors are known as content writers and content editors, although their roles vary from their print-based counterparts.

### Advertising

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Advertising")]

Advertising can provide income or a subsidized income for publishers. If the advertising has a [return on investment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return_on_investment "Return on investment") (ROI), the publisher can boost income exponentially by increasing the spending. An ROI of up to £10 per £1 invested is possible, as seen in the John Lewis & Partners [Christmas campaigns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lewis_Christmas_advert "John Lewis Christmas advert").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-21) Likewise, any cost savings that harm the customer/consumer experience can impact a brand in the long term. [Multichannel marketing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multichannel_marketing "Multichannel marketing") can be more cost-effective in creating an immersive experience that cannot be replicated with one channel. For example, when considering marketing spend, a shop with a small margin (or none at all) compared to a website is very cost-effective because it acts as a huge billboard that offers a browsing experience that enables consumers to make purchasing decisions. It gives them a feel for the brand, has a presence in the community, and creates jobs. Also, using social media publishing to advertise has a good ROI if trending, high-quality content is created that reflects positively on the brand.

### Tie-in publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Tie-in publishing")]

Main article: [Tie-in](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tie-in "Tie-in")

Film, television, radio, and advertisements publish information to their audiences. Computer games, streaming apps, and social media publish content in various ways that can keep audiences more engaged. Marketing additional products closely related to a major film, such as _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_, is an example of tie-in publishing. These products include but are not limited to spin-off books, graphic novels, soundtrack albums, computer games, models and toys, social media posts, and promotional publications. Examples of tie-in publishing based on books are the _[Harry Potter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter "Harry Potter")_ and _[James Bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James\_Bond "James Bond")_ franchises.

See also: [Periodical publication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodical_publication "Periodical publication")

The publishing landscape is continually evolving. Currently there are four major types of publishers in book publishing:[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-22)

### Mainstream publishers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Mainstream publishers")]

These companies traditionally produce hardcopy books in large print runs. They have established networks which distribute those books to bricks-and-mortar stores and libraries.

When a mainstream publisher accepts a book for publication, they require the author to sign a contract surrendering some rights to the publisher. In exchange, the publisher will take care of all aspects of publishing the book at the publisher's cost. They rely entirely on sales of the book to recoup those costs and make a profit. The author receives a royalty on each sale (and sometimes an advance on royalties when the book is accepted[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-23)). Because of the [financial risk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_risk "Financial risk"), mainstream publishers are extremely selective in what they will publish, and reject most manuscripts submitted to them.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-24)

In 2013, [Penguin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Group "Penguin Group") (owned by [Pearson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longman "Longman")) and [Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random_House "Random House") (owned by [Bertelsmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertelsmann_Stiftung "Bertelsmann Stiftung")) merged, narrowing the mainstream publishing industry to a handful of big publishers as it adapted to digital media.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-Penguin_Random_House_to_Buy_Simon_&_Schuster-25) The merger created the largest consumer book publisher globally, with a global market share of more than 25 percent.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-26)As of 2022[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit), approximately 80% percent of the United States trade market for books was controlled by the "**Big Five**" publishing houses: [Penguin Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Random_House "Penguin Random House"), [Hachette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hachette_Book_Group_USA "Hachette Book Group USA"), [HarperCollins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HarperCollins "HarperCollins"), [Simon & Schuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_&_Schuster "Simon & Schuster"), and [Macmillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macmillan_Publishers "Macmillan Publishers").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-27)

In November 2020, ViacomCBS agreed to sell Simon & Schuster, the third largest book publisher in the United States, to Penguin Random House in a deal that, if it had gone through, would have formed the largest publishing company in the world.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-Penguin_Random_House_to_Buy_Simon_&_Schuster-25) On November 2, 2021, the [United States Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice "United States Department of Justice") filed a lawsuit (U.S. v. Bertelsmann SE & CO. KGaA, et al.) to block the merger on antitrust grounds,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-28) and on October 31, 2022, the [D.C. District Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_District_Court_for_the_District_of_Columbia "United States District Court for the District of Columbia") ruled in favor of the Department of Justice, filing a permanent injunction on the merger.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-Judge_Blocks_a_Merger_of_Penguin_Random_House_and_Simon_&_Schuster-29)

Although newspaper and magazine companies still often own printing presses and binderies, book publishers rarely do.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Similarly, the trade usually sells the finished products through a [distributor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distribution_(business) "Distribution (business)") who stores and distributes the publisher's wares for a percentage fee or sells on a sale or return basis.

Some major publishers have entire divisions devoted to a single franchise, e.g., Ballantine [Del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Del_Rey_Books "Del Rey Books") LucasBooks has the exclusive rights to _Star Wars_ in the United States; Random House UK (Bertelsmann)/Century LucasBooks holds the same rights in the United Kingdom. The [video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") industry self-publishes through BL Publishing/[Black Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Library "Black Library") ([_Warhammer_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warhammer_Fantasy_(setting) "Warhammer Fantasy (setting)")) and Wizards of the Coast (_[Dragonlance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragonlance "Dragonlance")_, _[Forgotten Realms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forgotten\_Realms "Forgotten Realms")_, etc.). The [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") has its own publishing division that does very well with long-running series such as _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Who "Doctor Who")_. These multimedia works are cross-marketed aggressively, and sales frequently outperform the average stand-alone published work, making them a focus of corporate interest.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-cave-30)

The advent of the [Internet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet "Internet") has provided an alternative mode of book distribution and most mainstream publishers also offer their books in ebook format. Preparing a book for e-book publication is the same as print publication, with only minor variations in the process to account for the different publishing mediums; E-book publication also eliminates some costs like the discount given to retailers (usually around 45 percent).[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-ireaderreview.com-31)

### Small presses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Small presses")]

Small publishers, also called independent or indie publishers,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-32) operate on a traditional model (i.e. the author surrenders some rights in exchange for the publisher bearing all costs of publishing), but their precise terms can vary greatly.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-33) Often, they do not pay an advance on royalties.

### [Hybrid publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_publishing "Hybrid publishing")

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Hybrid publishing")]

A hybrid publisher shares the costs of publication (and therefore the risks) with the author. Because of this financial risk, they are selective in what they publish. The contract varies according to what is negotiated between author and company, but will always include the surrender of some rights to the publisher.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-34) Hybrid publishing is the source of debate in the publishing industry, due to the tendency of vanity presses to masquerade as hybrids.

### [Vanity presses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity_press "Vanity press")

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Vanity presses")]

A vanity press will publish any book. In return, the author must cover all the costs of publication, surrender some rights to the publisher, and pay royalties on sales. Vanity presses often engage in deceptive practices or offer costly, poor-quality services with limited recourse available to the writer. In the US, these practices have been cited by the [Better Business Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Better_Business_Bureau "Better Business Bureau") as unfavorable reports by consumers.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-35) Given the bad reputation of vanity publishing, many vanity presses brand themselves as hybrid publishers. The Society of Authors (SoA) and the Writers' Guild of Great Britain (WGGB) have called for reform of the paid-for publishing sector. These unions, representing 14,800 authors, jointly published a report to expose widespread bad practices among companies that charge writers to publish their work while taking away their rights.

### [Self-publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-publishing "Self-publishing")

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Self-publishing")]

When an author self-publishes a book, they retain all rights and assume responsibility for all stages of preparing, publishing and distributing the book. The author may hire professionals on a fee-for-service basis as needed, (e.g. an editor, cover designer, proofreader) or engage a company to provide an integrated package.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-36)

## Recent developments

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Publishing&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Recent developments")]

[Accessible publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accessible_publishing "Accessible publishing") uses the digitization of books to mark them up into [XML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XML "XML") and produce multiple formats to sell to customers, often targeting those who experience difficulty reading. Formats include a variety of larger print sizes, specialized print formats for [dyslexia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dyslexia "Dyslexia"),[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-37) eye tracking problems, and [macular degeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macular_degeneration "Macular degeneration"), as well as [Braille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braille "Braille"), [DAISY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_accessible_information_system "Digital accessible information system"), [audiobooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audiobook "Audiobook"), and [e-books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-books "E-books").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-38)

Green publishing means adapting the publishing process to minimize environmental impact. One example is the concept of on-demand printing, using digital or print-on-demand technology. This cuts down the need to ship books since they are manufactured close to the customer on a just-in-time basis.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-39)

A further development is the growth of online publishing, where no physical books are produced. The author creates an e-book and uploads it to a website, from which anyone can download and read it.

An increasing number of authors are using [niche marketing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niche_marketing "Niche marketing") online to sell more books by engaging with their readers online.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-40)

Some publishers can show political [homophily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homophily "Homophily") or [political bias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_bias "Political bias").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers#cite_note-p016-41)
